hints: Each alignment sums products of one signal value and one mask value.
Reverse the mask so those products appear at the same convolution coefficient.
Compute the convolution with FFT or exact number-theoretic transforms.
analogy: Reversing the mask turns a sliding dot product into ordinary polynomial multiplication.
example: For signal [1,2] and mask [3,4], the overlap sums from left to right are 4, 11, 6.
algorithm: Reverse the mask and convolve it with the signal. Print all n+m-1 coefficients in order. Use a sufficiently precise FFT and round to integers, or use an NTT modulus large enough to hold the maximum coefficient.
correctness: Coefficient t sums signal[i]*reversedMask[t-i], exactly the products of entries aligned at the corresponding shift, including partial overlaps at both ends.
complexity: For signal length n and mask length m, O((n+m) log(n+m)) time and O(n+m) space.
